Confidence Interval Interface - Common Arguments

Source: R/interfaceConfidenceIntervals.R
ConfidenceIntervals.Rd

Common confidence interval interface shared by multiple functions.

Arguments

conf.level

confidence level of the interval. If set to NA (which is the default) no confidence interval will be calculated.

sides

character string specifying the side of the confidence interval, must be one of "two.sided" (default), "left" or "right". The value names the side on which the finite bound lies. You can specify just the initial letter.

method

character string defining the type of interval required. The value should be one of "classic" or "boot" (default). Further arguments for the bootstrap procedure (such as R, type, etc.) can be supplied via the ... argument if needed.

Details

If conf.level = NA, no confidence interval is computed and only the point estimate is returned.

The sides argument controls whether a two-sided or one-sided confidence interval is calculated. It names the side on which the finite bound lies:

"left"

\([lci, \infty)\) - the left bound is finite, the interval is unbounded to the right.

"right"

\((-\infty, uci]\) - the right bound is finite, the interval is unbounded to the left.

Where the parameter is itself bounded, the unbounded side is reported at that boundary rather than as infinite: ccc, for instance, reports 1 and -1 in place of \(\infty\) and \(-\infty\).

Read this way, "left" corresponds to a hypothesis of "greater" in t.test and "right" to one of "less". Note that this is the reverse of the convention in DescTools, where sides names the direction of the alternative hypothesis instead. Code carrying one-sided intervals over from DescTools therefore needs its sides argument swapped; the change is silent, since both packages accept the same values.

Partial matching of the initial letter is supported.

The available method options may vary between functions, depending on the underlying statistic and its theoretical properties. Classical intervals typically rely on asymptotic normality or analytic variance formulas. Bootstrap intervals, specified via "boot", provide a broadly applicable alternative that can be used for a wide range of statistics without requiring closed-form variance expressions.

Bootstrap confidence intervals are computed using functionality from the boot package (see boot and boot.ci). Important parameters such as the number of resamples R and the bootstrap interval type ("perc", "bca", etc.) can be controlled via additional arguments.
